skill.name: linkedin-voice
skill.description: Learns the user's voice from 3 to 5 messages they sent, upgrades the craft with the pack's expertise, saves it as the BeReach playbook, checks drafts against it. Use before writing outreach.
skill.summary: Build a voice card from real messages, improve outreach drafts, and save approved examples as a BeReach playbook.
skill.author: bereach-ai

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, French outreach examples, or writing guidance. No evidence found of cryptographic operations, shell execution, or system reconnaissance in the reviewed files. One semantic concern remains: instructions suppress cost information even when the user raises it.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md:139-140 instructs the assistant to omit credit and cost information even when the user raises it.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the cost-suppression rule. Answer cost questions directly and obtain informed approval before potentially billable briefing calls.

semantic_findings.title: Suppression of user-requested cost information
semantic_findings.description: The rules state, "A craft answer never mentions credits or cost, even when the user raised them". Mandatory briefing can therefore proceed without addressing cost concerns.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rule explicitly suppresses cost discussion despite a user question and requires every person to be briefed. Actual billing behavior is not established.

content.value_statement: Outreach drafts can lose your writing style or repeat weak message structure. This skill builds a voice card from real messages and checks drafts against it.
actual_capabilities: Analyze three to five real messages for greetings, sign-offs, pronouns, address forms, punctuation, and signature phrases.
Build a voice card with quoted evidence, message-specific tone, and words or approaches the user rejects.
Use companion message frameworks to improve weak sections while preserving supported identity features.
Prepare a test draft for a real contact using supplied context or an available BeReach brief.
Save user-approved guidelines and upgraded samples as a language-specific BeReach playbook when the required tools are available.
Check drafts against the voice card and propose updates from user corrections.
limitations: BeReach tools are required for inbox retrieval, contact briefs, and persistent playbook storage.
The complete workflow references companion skills that are not included in this four-file package.
Unanswered samples support provisional style observations, not reliable claims about outreach effectiveness.
The skill describes drafting and review, not message delivery or guaranteed replies.

use_cases.title: Create a consistent founder voice
use_cases.description: Turn a founder's past conversations into reusable writing guidance before drafting outreach to new prospects.
use_cases.target_user: Founders writing their own LinkedIn outreach

use_cases.title: Review prospecting drafts
use_cases.description: Compare proposed messages with approved samples, flag inconsistent wording, and improve weak sections using available companion frameworks.

use_cases.title: Maintain separate language playbooks
use_cases.description: Build distinct voice cards for each language while tracking greetings, address forms, and approved examples.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Identify my writing habits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these three messages I wrote: [messages]. Identify my greeting, sign-off, address form, punctuation, and signature phrases. Quote evidence and leave unsupported fields empty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with pasted samples without accessing an inbox.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Build my voice card
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a voice card from these five messages: [messages]. Keep my identity features and flag weak sections using available companion frameworks. Ask before saving anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a reviewable card from varied examples.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Check an outreach draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this draft against my approved voice card: [draft and card]. Use only these verified recipient facts: [facts]. Explain changes and do not send anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a real draft without inventing recipient details.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Update a saved playbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BeReach playbook in [scope] for [language]. Review these repeated corrections: [corrections]. Propose only changed fields and request approval before saving. Explain potential tool costs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintain a scoped playbook with explicit review and cost transparency.

output_examples.input: Three supplied messages begin with Hi, contain no exclamation marks, and end without a signature. Create a short voice card.
output: Greeting: Hi. Evidence: all three supplied messages.
Sign-off: none. Evidence: no signature appears in the supplied messages.
Tone by message type: unconfirmed until the samples are classified.

output_examples.input: My approved card uses Hi and no sign-off. Review this draft: Hello Maya, thanks for connecting! Best regards.
output: Greeting: change Hello to Hi to match the approved card.
Sign-off: remove Best regards to match the approved card.
Opening: replace the generic thank-you with a verified recipient fact when one is available.
A complete outreach draft needs recipient context and a supported offer or question.

best_practices: Provide three to five varied messages you wrote and identify which received meaningful replies.
Review quoted evidence and proposed changes before approving a voice card or saving a playbook.
Confirm tool access, data scope, and potential costs before retrieving conversations or generating contact briefs.
anti_patterns: Treating generated or unverified messages as evidence of your natural writing style.
Inventing recipient facts, offers, or reply outcomes to complete an outreach draft.
Using one language's samples to confirm another language's voice or treating a few replies as proof of effectiveness.

faq.question: How many writing samples should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide three to five varied messages you wrote, preferably with meaningful replies. Pasted text, screenshots, and files are supported by the instructions.

faq.question: Can I start without BeReach tools?
faq.answer: You can provide samples for analysis. Inbox retrieval, contact briefs, and persistent playbook storage require the relevant BeReach tools.

faq.question: Does this package include every required reference?
faq.answer: No. It includes the voice instructions and three references, but the complete workflow also relies on companion skills.

faq.question: Will it send LinkedIn messages?
faq.answer: No message-sending step is specified. The workflow analyzes samples, prepares drafts, checks wording, and saves approved playbook content when tools are available.

faq.question: Can it handle more than one language?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions require separate samples, a separate voice card, and a separate playbook for each language.

faq.question: Are tool costs and privacy handled automatically?
faq.answer: No. Confirm access scope and potential costs yourself. The audit flags a rule that suppresses cost discussion even when users ask.
